target_customer: Consumers who want to sell used items from a phone
problem: Listing an item for sale takes typing, photos and categorizing; SimplyListed aimed to list an item automatically from one photo.
business_model: Consumer marketplace tool; monetization not stated in sources
product_category: Mobile resale listing app with computer vision

founders.name: Jon Grall
founders.background_notes: YC page describes a serial app developer and user-centered design expert with a 20-year software career across Silicon Valley startups and Fortune 100 companies; no employers or schools named. The YC page lists only one founder while team size is 2.

exit.reason: Not public; YC lists the company as inactive.

technical_complexity.rationale: Automatically creating a listing from a photo needs image recognition on a 2011 iPhone app, which was hard for two people but a narrow problem.

defensibility.rationale: No data or network effect is described; a prototype iPhone app released in February 2011 was easy for larger marketplaces to imitate.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source describes what incumbents did in response; not found.

market_need_then: The YC description states the premise that selling stuff online is a hassle; no spend, complaint or demand data was found for 2011.

identity.voice_and_tone: One-liner on YC is 'Sell your stuff.'

brand_strength.rationale: No press, logo description or community found; the name is descriptive and shares letters with several similarly named real estate and listing companies in search results.

outcome_analysis: SimplyListed was a two person YC W11 team building a photo-to-listing iPhone app whose prototype reached the App Store in February 2011. YC now marks it inactive, but no funding, traction, shutdown notice or post-mortem was found in any search, so the cause of the end is not public and no failure factors are asserted.
notes: The company has no listed website. No funding data found in several searches; unknown is not zero. No dated competitors found near the 2011 batch (one search for Craigslist alternatives returned only current roundups), so the list is empty. Similar names in search results (Sold, acquired by Dropbox in 2013; Listed; Simply Listed on Crunchbase) are different companies.
